body.value: There are a number of steps to take if you become unemployed.
Start with Intreo or the Department of Social Protection (DSP)

Intreo or the Department of Social Protection (DSP) is the main entry point for jobseeker payments and employment supports.

  1. Apply online for a jobseeker’s payment on MyWelfare.ie (you’ll most likely need a verified MyGovID).
  2. If you can’t apply online, you can:
  • Apply in person at your Intreo Centre
  • Request a paper form (UP1) by emailing jobseekersforms@welfare.ie.

It's important to note that Jobseeker’s Benefit is based on PRSI contributions, while Jobseeker’s Allowance is means-tested.
If you’re in immediate financial difficulty, contact Community Welfare Service (CWS)

The Community Welfare Service (CWS) can handle urgent/short-term supports under the Supplementary Welfare Allowance system, including Additional Needs Payments, which help with essentials like bills, clothing and so on, depending on circumstances).

Check how ton access CWS (you may not need an appointment; forms can be posted/dropped into Intreo offices and local CWS emails are listed per office).

If you need help with essential costs, look at Additional Needs Payment and apply online via MyWelfare or by post.

If you need housing cost support short-term, see Rent Supplement (where it applies).
Contact Revenue and sort out your tax if you stop working

You may be owed a tax/USC refund if you’re unemployed, and you can manage/close old employments if needed.

  1. Sign into Revenue's myAccount and use “Claim unemployment repayment” (PAYE Services).
  2. If your old employer hasn’t updated that you left, you can use myAccount to cease your old job.
  3. If you can’t do it online, Revenue notes you can use Form P50 via your Revenue office for unemployment repayment claims.
Look to housing support if needed

For longer-term rent support like Housing Assistance Payment (HAP), you generally need to be qualified for social housing and on the housing list. This is handled by your local authority.

  1. If you need support with rent, check HAP rules and process.
  2. If you’re not already on the council housing list, start with applying for social housing through your local authority.
  3. Then pursue HAP through your local authority.
Check health supports from the Health Service Executive (HSE)

If your income drops, you may qualify for a medical card (or GP visit card), and the HSE provides the application routes and support line.

  1. Apply online (where available) or use the HSE’s application options.
  2. If you need a form posted out or have questions, HSE lists a phone contact for medical card applications.
Get free guidance and advocacy help

Free guidance and advocacy help is very useful if forms get complicated.

For example, the Money Advice and Budgeting Service (MABS) offers free help with debt/budgeting if money is getting tight.
If you’re refused a payment, you can appeal
Contact the Social Welfare Appeals Office, which is independent of the Department of Social Protection.
